description: The objective of this course is to give students a clear understanding of concepts of formal languages, grammars and formal methods of computation.

syllabus.title: Finite Automata
syllabus.body: Introduction to Finite State Machine, Moore and Mealy FSMs, equivalence, minimal finite automata, unions, intersections and complement of FA, NFA, NFA with null transitions.

syllabus.title: Regular Languages
syllabus.body: Regular expressions, criterion for regularity, the pumping lemma, decision problems, equivalence of FA and regular expressions, Arden's theorem, non-determinism and Kleene's theorem.

syllabus.title: Context-Free Grammars
syllabus.body: Definition of CFG, derivation tree, ambiguity, CNF, GNF, pushdown automata, PDA to CFG and vice versa, pumping lemma for CFG.

syllabus.title: Turing Machines
syllabus.body: Turing Machine definition and as language acceptors, recursively enumerable and recursive languages, Chomsky hierarchy, halting problem, Post correspondence problem, Rice theorem, P and NP, polynomial-time reductions and NP-Completeness.

outcomes: Understand the foundations of finite automata (deterministic or non-deterministic), FSM and master regular languages.
Be exposed to types of languages (type-0 to type-3), context-free languages and pushdown automata as their acceptor.
Design Turing machines for various mathematical and string functions.
Demonstrate the concept of decidability, unsolvability and recursive languages.
referenceBooks: John C. Martin, Introduction to Languages and the Theory of Computation, MGH.
J.E. Hopcroft and J.D. Ullman, Introduction to Automata Theory Languages and Computation, Narosa.
